answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because sparrow only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, knoll is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any pearl approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
